newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 23.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 23.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Lumber prices were mixed in early trading. Most prices in the West and in Western Canada drifted lower, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Strength continued in Southern Pine, though westside prices flattened, the reporting agency said.

Producers were not apt to chop prices, believing just-in-time buying and healthy consumption could soon force buyers to replenish. However, counters, tally adjustments, or other concessions were common, as buyers found supplies readily available. Sales of structural panels were spotty, Random Lengths said.

Western S-P-F prices drifted in slow trading. Monday's limit-down move in futures reinforced buyers' bearish attitudes. A pick up in sales Tuesday encouraged producers, with many focusing on #2&Btr 2x6. Std&Btr 2x4 softened, with pressure coming from 8/16' tallies offered in the $340s.
2x6 quotes reached the high $360s. Cracks showed in 2x10 and 2x12 prices, as Hem-Fir offerings undercut S-P-F prices.

Eastern S-P-F trading was sporadic to slow. Mill orders ran heavy to back-to-back purchasing, with mixed specifications and fast shipments two keys. Wholesalers and distributors sold from skimpy inventories and replaced in small volumes. Prices were flat on most items. Exceptions were #1&2 2x4 in the Northeast, up $5, and 2x4 precut studs, which regained strength.
Southern Pine continued to move well, albeit at a slightly slower pace, Random Lengths said.
